translationRepairs: Emperor Muzong, Filial, Peaceful, Reverent, and Upright, whose personal name was Jing and whose courtesy name was Shulü.
Emperor Muzong, Filial, Peaceful, Reverent, and Upright, whose personal name was Jing and whose childhood name was Shulü.
s0002 has 小字述律; 小字 is a childhood/pet name, not a courtesy name (字), so replacing 'courtesy name' with 'childhood name' corrects a real terminological error.
Emperor Muzong, Filial, Peaceful, Reverent, and Upright — personal name Jing, courtesy name Shulü.
Emperor Muzong, Filial, Peaceful, Reverent, and Upright — personal name Jing, childhood name Shulü.
The same 小字述律 governs the literal field; 'courtesy name' misreads 小字 as 字, and 'childhood name' is the accurate rendering.
In the ninth month, on bingchen day, as Zhou invaded Han, Han sent envoys to report the attack.
In the ninth month, on bingshen day, as Zhou invaded Han, Han sent envoys to report the attack.
s0078 dates the event 九月丙申; 丙申 is bingshen, whereas bingchen would be 丙辰, so the proposed day name matches the Chinese.
In the ninth month, on bingchen day, Han, invaded by the people of Zhou, sent envoys to report it.
In the ninth month, on bingshen day, Han, invaded by the people of Zhou, sent envoys to report it.
The literal likewise must follow 丙申 as bingshen, not bingchen (丙辰).
That autumn, in the seventh month on gengchen day, the ruler of Han fell ill and sent envoys to announce it.
That autumn, in the ninth month on gengchen day, the ruler of Han fell ill and sent envoys to announce it.
s0089 opens 秋九月庚辰; 九月 is the ninth month, so the original 'seventh month' is a factual mistranslation and the proposed ninth month is correct.
In the seventh month of autumn, on gengchen day, the Han ruler fell ill and sent envoys to report it.
In the ninth month of autumn, on gengchen day, the Han ruler fell ill and sent envoys to report it.
The literal must likewise render 九月 as the ninth month of autumn, not the seventh.
That winter, in the eleventh month, on renchen day, the Biegude brought tribute.
That winter, in the eleventh month, on renyin day, the Biegude brought tribute.
s0101 has 冬十一月壬寅; 壬寅 is renyin, whereas renchen would be 壬辰, so the replacement day name is accurate.
In the eleventh month of winter, on day renchen, the Biegude came to pay tribute.
In the eleventh month of winter, on day renyin, the Biegude came to pay tribute.
The same 壬寅 requires renyin in the literal field; renchen (壬辰) is the wrong stem-branch reading.
